## 一、核心概括

现有资料未涵盖越南《企业法》本身，但依据越南邮电部《Circular No. 06/2000/TT-TCBD》【来源1】，外资参与邮政、电信、互联网业务时，公司治理结构存在**所有制形式限制**：多数需许可业务要求国有企业或国家持主导/特别股的股份公司形态，外资企业实际上被排除在特定业务之外，或须通过合资形式接受国家持股安排。

## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 需许可业务的所有制形式限制

**法规出处**：越南《Circular No. 06/2000/TT-TCBD》第2.2条【来源1】。

**深度解读**：该条规定，从事第2.1条(a)至(d)项业务——即建设国家电信骨干网、公共电信网并提供电信服务，建设互联网网络并提供IAP/ISP服务，建设邮政网并提供邮政服务，以及邮票印刷——的企业，必须是**国有企业**或**国家持有主导股或特别股的股份公司**。这意味着外资企业在上述核心业务领域无法以100%外资独资形式运营，只能通过与国家持股的合资股份公司参与，且国家须保持控制性持股。立法意图在于确保邮政电信这一涉及国家安全和公共利益的行业由国家保持主导权。

**重点提示**：该限制仅适用于第2.1条(a)-(d)项业务；第2.1条(e)项（无线电发射机及收发机制造）则明确"任何经济成分的企业"均可经营，外资在此领域不受所有制限制。此外，企业须先完成商业登记，再申请许可证，取得许可证后方可开始经营。

**实务指引**：外资拟进入越南电信核心业务，应优先设计**合资股份公司**架构，在股东协议和公司章程中明确国家持股比例安排；同时核实目标业务是否落入第2.1条(a)-(d)项范围。常见误区是认为取得投资登记即可运营，实际上还须另行申请行业许可证。

### 2. 无需许可业务对外资的开放

**法规出处**：越南《Circular No. 06/2000/TT-TCBD》第3.1、3.2条【来源1】。

**深度解读**：第3.1条列举了无需许可证的条件类业务，包括：邮政电信物资设备制造（不含无线电收发机）、进出口、购销、邮政电信服务代理、外国快递公司代理、邮票及集邮品进出口购销等。第3.2条明确"在越南合法经营的各种经济成分的企业"均可注册经营上述业务，自满足条件并承诺持续维持条件之时起即有权经营。这为外资企业提供了相对开放的准入空间，但"条件"本身构成实质性门槛。

**重点提示**：无需许可不等于无监管——企业须**持续维持**业务条件，并遵守商品服务质量、信息广告、赔偿处理等相关法律规定【来源1】。条件一旦丧失，经营资格即受影响。

**实务指引**：外资进入此类业务应建立**条件合规台账**，逐项对照第3.4至3.9条的具体条件（如标准符合性认证、货物标签、代理合同要素等），并保留持续合规证据。建议在投资前完成条件差距分析，避免注册后无法实际运营。

### 3. 代理关系中的治理与合同要求

**法规出处**：越南《Circular No. 06/2000/TT-TCBD》第3.7、3.8条【来源1】。

**深度解读**：从事邮政电信服务代理，须与持牌服务提供企业或转售企业签订代理合同，合同须明确**代理服务种类、质量、资费及佣金比例**；代理场所须标示委托方的商号和标识，并接受邮电总局的检查监督。外国快递公司代理则要求代理方本身须持有国际邮政服务许可证，且外国委托方须为与越南建有国际邮政关系国家的合法持牌企业，代理活动须确保国家主权、安全及用户利益。

**重点提示**：外国快递代理的框架合同须向邮电总局**登记备案**，交易文书须以越南语和一门外语表述；还须在交易场所公示资费、质量指标及用户权利义务，并按要求提交年度或临时报告。

**实务指引**：外资通过代理模式进入时，应将代理合同的核心要素（服务范围、质量标准、佣金）条款化，完成框架合同登记，并建立定期报告机制。常见误区是忽视合同登记和公示义务，导致合规瑕疵。

### 4. 许可申请的程序性治理要求

**法规出处**：越南《Circular No. 06/2000/TT-TCBD》第2.3、2.4条【来源1】。

**深度解读**：企业须先依法完成商业登记，再申请许可证。以无线电收发机制造许可为例，申请材料包括申请书、企业组织与运营章程、生产方案（设备类别、技术性能、频率频段、发射功率、工艺及产能等）。邮电总局须在收到有效材料后**45日内**完成评估发证，需复核的可延长但不超过**60日**；拒发的须在上述期限内书面答复。

**重点提示**：组织与运营章程是审查重点，直接关系公司治理结构的合规性；时限为行政机关办理期限，企业应预留材料补正时间。

**实务指引**：建议在章程中预先体现符合第2.2条所有制要求的股权结构，并准备完整生产方案。若涉外资，应同步核查投资登记与商业登记的衔接。

### 5. 资料不足之处

关于越南《企业法》对**外资企业**公司治理结构（如董事会构成、法定代表人居留要求、股东会表决机制等）的直接规定，**现有法规资料暂未提供明确规定**。上述分析仅基于邮电电信领域条件业务的行业性规范【来源1】，不能替代对《企业法》本身的核查。来源2仅涉及电信业务定义，来源3仅涉及服务质量重新登记，均未涉及公司治理。

## 三、总结与建议

现有资料显示，外资在越南邮政电信互联网领域的治理限制主要体现为**所有制形式门槛**：核心电信、互联网及邮政网络业务须由国家控股的国企或股份公司经营，外资须以合资形式参与；制造、进出口、代理等业务则向各种经济成分开放，但须持续满足条件并履行合同登记、公示、报告等治理性义务。建议：第一，投资前逐项比对第2.1条与第3.1条，确定目标业务是否需许可及所有制限制；第二，在章程和代理合同中预先嵌入合规要素；第三，就《企业法》层面的外资治理要求，另行核查越南《企业法》及配套法令的现行文本。

THE GENERAL DEPARTMENT OF POST AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS
CIRCULAR No. 06/2000/TT-TCBD OF SEPTEMBER 29, 2000 GUIDING THE ACTIVITIES REGARDING THE CONDITIONAL BUSINESS LINES IN THE DOMAINS
OF POST, TELECOMMUNICATIONS AND INTERNET

In furtherance of the provisions of Decree No. 03/2000/ND-CP of February 3, 2000 guiding the implementation of a number of articles
of the Enterprises Law and Decree No. 30/2000/ND-CP of August 11, 2000 on the cancellation of a number of permits and licenses and
the conversion of a number of licenses into business conditions and, at the same time, in order to create favorable conditions for
activities of enterprises; after consulting with several concerned ministries and branches, the General Department of Post and Telecommunications
hereby guides a number of contents of business activities in the domains of post, telecommunications and internet as follows:
I. GENERAL PROVISIONS


1.1 This Circular provides guidance for enterprises engaged in business activities in the domain of post and telecommunications and
Internet, as prescribed by law, which fall under the conditional business lines.
1.2 Post and/or telecommunications enterprises are enterprises engaged in business activities in one or several domains prescribed
in the Government�s Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP of November 12, 1997 on post and telecommunications. The conditional post and telecommunication
business lines include:
a/ Provision of postal and telecommunication services;
b/ Manufacture of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;


c/ Import, export, purchase and sale of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;
d/ Printing of postage stamps; production, import, export, purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage
stamps.
1.3 Internet services-providing enterprises are enterprises dealing in Internet services specified in the Government�s Decree No.
21/CP of March 5, 1997 issuing the Provisional Regulation on the management, establishment and use of the Internet in Vietnam".
The conditional Internet business lines include:
a/ Provision of Internet access services (IAP);
b/ Provision of Internet services (ISP).


1.4 The postal, telecommunication and Internet domains fall under the conditional business lines, where some business domains require
permits of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications while some others do not but must satisfy the conditions set in
this Circular.
1.5 Various kinds of permits and certificates used for technical and professional management prescribed in Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP
in order to ensure the network and service quality, ensure safety for operation of public and exclusive postal and telecommunication
networks and ensure the interests of users shall not be regulated by this Circular.


II. CONDITIONS FOR BUSINESS LINES WHICH REQUIRE PERMITS
2.1 The post, telecommunication and Internet business lines that require permits include:
a/ Establishment of national telecommunication backbone networks, public telecommunication networks and provision (direct or for resale)
of telecommunication services (basic, value-added);
b/ Establishment of Internet networks and provision of Internet services (IAP and ISP);
c/ Establishment of postal networks and provision of postal services;
d/ Printing of postage stamps;
e/ Manufacture of radio transmitters and receivers-transmitters.


2.2. Enterprises conducting business activities in the domains specified at Points a, b, c and d, Section 2.1 shall be State enterprises
or joint-stock companies where the State holds the predominant or special shares. For the domain specified at Point e, Section 2.1,
the business subjects shall be enterprises of any economic sector. Enterprises may do business in these domains under conditions
and according to the operating duration specified in their permits and start their business activities only when they obtain their
licenses.


2.3. Enterprises must make business registration according to law provisions before carrying out procedures applying for permits to
do business in the domains specified at Point 2.1 above.
2.4. The conditions, order and procedures for granting of permits to do business in the domains specified at Point 2.1 above shall
be as follows:
a/ For permits stated at Point a , the provisions in Circular No. 04/1998/TT-TCBD of September 29, 1998 of the General Department
of Post and Telecommunications guiding the Government�s Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP of November 12, 1997 on telecommunication networks
and services, shall be complied with.


b/ For permits specified at Point b, the provisions of Joint Circular No. 08/TTLT of May 24, 197 of the General Department of Post
and Telecommunications, the Ministry of the Interior (now the Ministry of Public Security) and the Ministry of Culture and Information
guiding the licensing of the connection, provision and use of Internet in Vietnam, shall be complied with;


c/ For permits specified at Point c, the provisions of Circular No. 02/1998/TT-TCBD of June 20, 1998 of the General Department of
Post and Telecommunications guiding the implementation of the Government�s Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP on postal networks and services,
shall be complied with;
d/ For permits specified at Point d, the provisions of Decision No. 217/2000/QD-TCBD of March 6, 2000 of the General Department of
Post and Telecommunications issuing the Regulation on the professional management of postage stamps, shall be complied with.


e/ The order and procedures for licensing the manufacture of radio transmitters and/or receivers-transmitters:
- A dossier of application for permit shall consist of:
+ An application;
+ The enterprise�s organization and operation charter;
+ The production scheme with the following principal contents: category of equipment, technical properties (frequency, frequency band,
transmitting capacity of equipment�), technology and capacity of the production lines�


- Time limit for handling dossiers: The General Department of Post and Telecommunications shall evaluate and grant permits within
45 days after the receipt of valid dossiers. If there arise any matters which need to be re-examined, the above time-limit may be
extended but shall not exceed 60 days after receipt of valid dossiers. In case of refusal, the General Department of Post and Telecommunications
shall send written reply to the enterprise within the above time-limit.
III. CONDITIONS FOR BUSINESS LINES WHICH REQUIRE NO PERMIT
3.1 The conditional postal and telecommunication business lines which require no permit:


a/ Manufacture of post and telecommunication supplies and equipment (excluding radio transmitters and receivers-transmitters);
b/ Import and export of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;
c/ Purchase and sale of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;
d/ Postal and telecommunication service provision agency;
e/ Agency for foreign express mail service companies;
f/ Import, export, purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage stamps.


3.2. Enterprises of all economic sectors that legally operate in Vietnam may register and do business in the domains specified at
Point 3.1 and shall be entitled to do business in such domains from the time they satisfy all business conditions set in this Circular
and commit themselves to maintain these conditions throughout the process of business operation.
3.3. During the process of business operation, enterprises must comply with law provisions on the goods and services quality, regulations
on information and advertisement, regulations on settlement of compensation claims as well as other relevant law provisions.


3.4. Business conditions for the manufacture of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment:
a/ For supplies and equipment on the "List of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment subject to standard conformity
certification" issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications, enterprises shall have to carry out the standard
conformity certification procedures for such supplies and equipment before circulating them on the market.


The order, procedures and conditions for standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment
are prescribed in the Regulation on the standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment,
issued together with Decision No. 285/2000/QD-TCBD of March 29, 2000 of the General Director of Post and Telecommunications.
b/ For subscribed terminal devices, enterprises shall have to effect the goods labeling thereof according to Circular No. 03/2000/TT-TCBD
of July 26, 2000 of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications.


3.5. Business conditions for the import and export of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment:
a/ For supplies and equipment on the "List of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment subject to standard conformity
certification", issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications, enterprises shall have to carry out the standard
conformity certification procedures for such supplies and equipment before importing them.


The order, procedures and conditions for standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment
are prescribed in the Regulation on the standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment,
issued together with Decision No. 285/2000/QD-TCBD of March 29, 2000 of the General Director of Post and Telecommunications.


b/ For foreign-made subscribed terminal devices which are imported for sale on the Vietnamese market, enterprises shall have to effect
the goods labeling thereof according to Circular No. 03/2000/TT-TCBD of July 26, 2000 of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications.


c/ For radio transmitters and receivers-transmitters, enterprises may import only those with a frequency or frequency band in line
with the planning on the allocation of the frequency spectrum to operations in Vietnam, issued together with the Prime Minister�s
Decision No. 85/1998/QD-TTg of April 16, 1998 approving Vietnam�s planning on the allocation of the frequency spectrum to operations
and other relevant regulations of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications;


d/ For fixed satellite transmitters, receiver-transmitters used in telecommunication operations and broadcasting operations, enterprises
shall have to request their customers wishing to use such equipment to apply for permits to use transmitters and radio frequencies,
issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications before carrying out import procedures;
e/ Enterprises shall have to notify customers of those kinds of radio transmitters, receiver-transmitters which require the Post and
Telecommunications General Department�s permits for use of radio transmitters and frequencies;


f/ The import and export of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment for security and defense purposes shall comply with
the regulations of the Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of Defense.
3.6. Business conditions for the purchase and sale of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment:


a/ For supplies and equipment on the "List of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment subject to standard conformity
certification", issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications, enterprises may only deal in the purchase
and sale of supplies and equipment already certified for their standard conformity as prescribed;
b/ For subscribed terminal devices, enterprises shall have to effect the goods labeling thereof according to Circular No. 03/2000/TT-TCBD
of July 26, 2000 of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications;


c/ For the purchase and sale of radio transmitters, receiver-transmitters, enterprises shall have to notify customers of those kinds
of radio transmitters, receiver-transmitters which require the Post and Telecommunications General Department�s licenses for use
of radio transmitters and frequencies;
3.7. Conditions for acting as postal and telecommunication service provision agents:


a/ Enterprises wishing to act as postal and telecommunication service provision agents must sign agency contracts with postal and
telecommunication service-providing enterprises or telecommunication service-reselling enterprises (hereinafter called the principals
for short). The agency contracts must clearly state kinds of postal and telecommunication services the agents are permitted to provide,
the quality and charge of each kind of service and the commission rate enjoyed by the agents.


b/ Pledge is made to provide the right services with proper quality as stated in the agency contracts and to collect charges at the
rates applied by the principals to users.
c/ Places of postal and telecommunication service provision agents must be put up with the commercial names and logos of the principals;


d/ Postal and telecommunication service provision agents must comply with the rules on postal and telecommunication services issued
by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications and submit to the inspection and supervision by the General Department of
Post and Telecommunications as well as competent State management bodies in the provision of postal and telecommunication services.
3.8. Conditions for acting as agents for foreign express mail service companies:


a/ Only enterprises licensed by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications to provide international postal services may
act as service agents (hereinafter called as agents for short) for foreign express mail service companies;
b/ Enterprises may sign agency contracts with foreign express mail service companies within the scope of international postal services
already licensed;
c/ Foreign express mail service companies that sign agency contracts must be those licensed to lawfully operate in one of the countries
with which Vietnam has established international post relations;


d/ Agency activities for foreign express mail service companies must ensure the national sovereignty and security as well as the interests
of service users and comply with the provisions of Vietnamese laws on post, tax, customs, information security and mail safety;


e/ Enterprises acting as agents for foreign express mail service companies, on the basis of Vietnamese laws and agreements with foreign
express mail service companies, shall have to formulate framework agency contracts for uniform application within the whole enterprises
and register such model contracts with the General Department of Post and Telecommunications; print matters used in transactions
with service users must be expressed in Vietnamese and a foreign language.


f/ Enterprises acting as agents for foreign express mail companies shall have to announce and post up at the transaction places the
service charges, service quality norms and users� rights and obligations;
g/ Enterprises acting as agents for foreign express mail service companies shall apply the annual regular or irregular regime of reporting
on the results of agency activities at the request of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications.
3.9. Conditions for conducting business in the import, export, purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity
postage stamps:


a/ Only enterprises licensed to do business in mail service may conduct import and export of postage stamps, stamp publications and
commodity postage stamps;
b/ Enterprises that deal in the purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage stamps must sign agency
contracts with mail service-providing enterprises;


c/ It is forbidden to purchase, sell, import or export any kind of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage stamps,
which the General Department of Post and Telecommunications have suspended from issuance, banned from circulation or which have unhealthy
contents, incite or sow hatred among nations, infringe upon the national sovereignty and run counter to the Vietnamese traditional
practices and laws.
IV. IMPLEMENTATION PROVISIONS
4.1. This Circular takes effect 15 days after its signing. All the previous provisions which are contrary to this Circular are now
annulled.


4.2. Units of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications shall, within the scope of their relevant powers and tasks, have
to explain, guide, inspect and supervise the implementation of this Circular.
4.3. Enterprises shall have to strictly abide by the provisions of this Circular. Any problems arising in the course of implementation
should be promptly reported by enterprises to the General Department of Post and Telecommunications for guidance or explanation.

## 一、核心概括（80-100字）

经核查现有法规资料，**未收录越南《招标法》（Law on Bidding）的任何条文**，因此无法就政府采购流程和投标人资质的具体规定给出有法条支撑的结论。以下基于资料库中与电信、互联网领域市场准入及代理经营相关的越南法规，梳理与“资质条件”“合同签订前置程序”相关的制度逻辑，供理解越南特许经营领域准入规则作参考，但不能等同于《招标法》的规定。

## 二、法律依据详解

**1. 资料库覆盖范围与结论边界说明**

1. 法规出处：现有资料包括越南《关于加强公共互联网代理点管理的指令》（07/2004/CT-BBCVT）【来源1】、《关于邮政、电信和信息技术组织与运作的第75/2003/ND-CP号法令》【来源2】、《关于〈商法〉国际货物买卖活动实施细则的第12/2006/ND-CP号法令》【来源3】、《关于邮政、电信和互联网领域有条件经营行业活动的第06/2000/TT-TCBD号通知》【来源4】以及《电信法》第63条【来源5】。
2. 深度解读：上述法规均属电信、邮政、互联网及商事领域，**不涉及政府采购招标程序**。越南《招标法》的适用范围、招标方式（公开招标、限制性招标、指定招标等）、投标人资格（财务能力、技术能力、经验要求）等核心内容，在现有资料中完全没有对应条文。
3. 重点提示：不得将电信领域的“许可证条件”直接类推为《招标法》下的“投标人资质”，二者法律性质不同——前者是行业准入许可，后者是采购程序中的资格评审。
4. 实务指引：如需准确回答该问题，应补充检索越南《招标法》（Luật Đấu thầu）现行文本及其配套法令（如关于投标人资格、招标程序细节的政府法令）。

**2. 越南特许经营领域的“资质前置”制度逻辑（可参考的类比制度）**

1. 法规出处：越南《第06/2000/TT-TCBD号通知》第2.1条、第2.2条、第2.3条【来源4】。
2. 深度解读：该通知将电信、互联网业务划分为“需许可证”与“无需许可证但需满足条件”两类。需许可证的业务（如建立互联网网络、提供IAP/ISP服务）要求企业**先完成工商登记，再申请许可证**，且部分领域限定为国家企业或国家持股主导的股份公司。这体现越南在关键基础设施领域“主体资格限定+许可前置”的监管思路。
3. 重点提示：许可证载明经营条件和经营期限，企业只能在取得许可证后方可开展业务【来源4】。
4. 实务指引：若参与越南政府相关项目，应先核查自身是否具备相应行业许可证及主体资格，再评估是否满足采购方的资格要求。

**3. 代理合同签订的前置登记要求（合同程序类比）**

1. 法规出处：越南《07/2004/CT-BBCVT号指令》第一部分a项、b项【来源1】。
2. 深度解读：该指令要求，拟提供公共互联网代理服务的用户，**须先依法完成互联网代理业务登记，之后才能与互联网服务提供商签订代理合同**。合同内容除一般合同条款外，还须加入代理业主的责任条款，包括张贴内部使用规定、登记线路号码、制止用户违规行为等。
3. 重点提示：代理业主若纵容或故意包庇窃取密码、传播病毒、访问淫秽内容等行为，构成提供商停止服务和暂停代理合同的依据【来源1】。
4. 实务指引：在越南开展代理类业务，应将“业务登记完成”作为签约的先决条件，并在合同中明确合规责任条款，避免因程序瑕疵导致合同被暂停。

**4. 合同履行监督与违规处理机制**

1. 法规出处：越南《07/2004/CT-BBCVT号指令》第一部分c项、d项及后续段落【来源1】。
2. 深度解读：提供商负有检查监督代理合同履行的义务；若有充分依据认定代理业主违规构成暂停合同的条件，应制作书面记录、停止服务并通知地方邮电部门。电信企业须配合提供商，在收到监察机构书面通知后断开违规代理点的电话线路或传输线路。
3. 重点提示：提供商若自身代理管理不达标，须**暂停签订新的代理合同**进行整顿，并向邮电部报告【来源1】。
4. 实务指引：建立合同履行的定期检查台账，保留书面记录，确保在触发暂停条件时有完整证据链。

**5. 法律实施的分层授权模式**

1. 法规出处：越南《电信法》第63条【来源5】、《第75/2003/ND-CP号法令》末条【来源2】。
2. 深度解读：越南立法普遍采用“国会立法+政府细化+部长指导实施”的分层模式。《电信法》第63条明确由政府细化指导实施【来源5】；《第75/2003/ND-CP号法令》则授权邮电部长指导实施【来源2】。这意味着《招标法》的具体程序规则很可能也由配套法令细化，仅查阅法律本身不足以掌握全貌。
3. 重点提示：研究越南《招标法》必须同步检索其配套政府法令和部长通知。
4. 实务指引：建议按“法律—政府法令—部级通知”三层结构系统检索，并关注现行有效版本及修订情况。

## 三、总结与建议（150-200字）

**结论**：现有法规资料未提供越南《招标法》的任何条文，无法就政府采购流程和投标人资质给出有法条支撑的答案。资料库中可参考的是电信、互联网领域的“许可前置+主体资格限定+合同登记”制度逻辑，但这属于行业准入监管，不能替代《招标法》的投标人资格评审规则。

**行动建议**：一是补充检索越南《招标法》（Luật Đấu thầu）及其配套法令原文；二是区分“行业许可证资质”与“投标人资格”两个不同法律概念；三是关注越南法律的分层授权结构，避免仅凭法律条文作片面判断。

yearDIRECTIVE No. 07/2004/CT-BBCVT OF JULY 19, 2004 ON ENHANCING THE MANAGEMENT OF PUBLIC INTERNET AGENTS
Over the recent years, Vietnam's Internet has witnessed a fast development and exerted positive impacts on various aspects of the
national socio-economic life, thus actually bringing about great efficacies and creating favorable conditions for and effectively
supporting the implementation of the open-door and proactive international economic integration policies of the Party and the State.


Together with the general development of Internet, public Internet agents have also actively contributed to the universalization of
Internet services to people of all strata. However, besides positive aspects of this mode of service provision, many public Internet
access spots, which are providing Internet services in form of Internet service agents, have failed to comply with the law provisions
on Internet management, letting users arbitrarily access unhealthy information which may cause harms to the political security, social
order and safety and national cultural identity of Vietnam.


In order to enhance the management of activities of public Internet agents in strict compliance with the provisions of the Government's
Decree No. 55/2001/ND-CP of August 23, 2001 on management, provision and use of Internet services, thus minimizing negative phenomena
which may occur in Internet agency activities, the Minister of Post and Telematics hereby instructs as follows:
Internet service providers (ISP) and telecommunications on-line service providers (OSP) shall:
a/ Notify and guide Internet service users who wish to provide public Internet services in making business registrations and signing


of agency contracts with Internet service providers. The signing of Internet agency contracts shall be effected only after the users
have registered the Internet agency business with the local business registries according to law provisions.
b/ Elaborate and promulgate the Regulation on management of Internet agents and model agency contracts for unified use by providers.
The providers' model Internet agency contracts must be sent to the Ministry of Post and Telematics. The contents of Internet agency
contracts, besides general law provisions on contracts, must be added with some points related to the responsibilities of agent owners,


more concretely as follows:
- Agent owners must post up internal regulations on the use of Internet services at their own establishments, which include the bans
prescribed in Article 11 of the Government's Decree No. 55/2001/ND-CP of August 23, 2001 on management, provision and use of Internet
services.
- Agent owners must register their telephone numbers or serial numbers of their contracts on hiring of telecommunications transmission
lines used for Internet access with Internet service providers.
- Internet agent owners must guide service users in complying with the regulations on Internet use. When detecting service users who


intentionally violate the regulations on Internet use or violate internal regulations on Internet service use, Internet agents shall
have to immediately stop the service users' violations.
- The agent owners' acts of facilitating or intentionally covering up acts of stealing passwords or access accounts; spreading viruses;
accessing electronic news pages or propagating or spreading documents with depraved or obscene contents, violating the fine customs
and traditions or infringing upon the national security, shall constitute grounds for providers to stop providing services and suspend
the agency contracts.


c/ Work out plans on, and take the initiative in conducting, the inspection and supervision of the performance of the signed contracts
by the Internet agents. In the course of inspection and supervision of the performance of agency contracts, if providers have enough
grounds to conclude that agent owners' violations of contract provisions constitute the conditions for suspending contracts, they
shall make written records thereon, stop providing services and concurrently send written notices on law violations by such agents
to the local Post and Telematics Departments or Services.


d/ Review the management of Internet agents by providers according to the contents of the Government's Decree No. 55/2001/ND-CP, the
guiding documents of the Ministry of Post and Telematics, the Ministry of Culture and Information and the Ministry of Public Security
as well as the provisions of this Directive, paying special attention to the agent management regulation; contents of agency contracts;
plans on supervision and inspection of contract performance by agents. Where they deem the agent management is not up to the set


requirements, providers shall have to temporarily suspend the signing of new Internet agency contracts for reorganizing their management
work and reporting such to the Ministry of Post and Telematics.
Telecommunications enterprises shall have to coordinate with Internet service providers in disconnecting Internet agents' telephone
numbers or telecommunications transmission lines for Internet access if they receive written notices of the Inspectorate of the Ministry
of Post and Telematics or the local Post and Telematics Departments or Services on law violations committed by agents and their requests


for disconnecting telephone numbers or telecommunications transmission lines for Internet access.
The Post and Telematics Ministry's Inspectorate shall expeditiously assume the prime responsibility for elaborating a joint circular
guiding Article 41 of the Government's Decree No. 55/2001/ND-CP of August 23, 2001 on Internet service management, provision and
use regarding violation acts, forms and levels of sanction against administrative violations in Internet domain. The Inspectorate
of the Ministry of Post and Telematics, the provincial/municipal Post and Telematics Departments and Services shall:


a/ Work out plans on, and conduct, inspection or examination of Internet service providers in the management of public Internet agents.
In the course of inspection or examination, if detecting that providers fail to meet the requirements of the agent management according
to regulations, the Inspectorate of the Ministry of Post and Telematics shall request in writing those providers to temporarily suspend
the signing of new agency contracts for reorganizing their agent management.
b/ Take initiative in coordinating with the local administrations and the concerned ministries and branches in organizing the inspection


of activities of public Internet agents, especially those in large cities like Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh city, Da Nang, Hai Phong, Can Tho,
etc.
c/ Resolutely sanction administrative violations committed by service providers and public Internet agents regarding law provisions
on Internet according to their respective State management competence and functions prescribed in the Ordinance on Handling of Administrative
Violations, the Government's Decree No. 142/2004/ND-CP and Decree No. 55/2001/ND-CP.
The Telecommunications Department shall coordinate with the concerned units under the Ministry of Culture and Information and the


Ministry of Public Security in studying and organizing the elaboration of a joint circular on management of public Internet agents
for promulgation in 2004.
The Minister of Post and Telematics shall request Internet service providers, telecommunications enterprises and concerned units to
strictly implement this Directive.
Minister of Post and Telematics
DO TRUNG TA

THE GENERAL DEPARTMENT OF POST AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS
CIRCULAR No. 06/2000/TT-TCBD OF SEPTEMBER 29, 2000 GUIDING THE ACTIVITIES REGARDING THE CONDITIONAL BUSINESS LINES IN THE DOMAINS
OF POST, TELECOMMUNICATIONS AND INTERNET

In furtherance of the provisions of Decree No. 03/2000/ND-CP of February 3, 2000 guiding the implementation of a number of articles
of the Enterprises Law and Decree No. 30/2000/ND-CP of August 11, 2000 on the cancellation of a number of permits and licenses and
the conversion of a number of licenses into business conditions and, at the same time, in order to create favorable conditions for
activities of enterprises; after consulting with several concerned ministries and branches, the General Department of Post and Telecommunications
hereby guides a number of contents of business activities in the domains of post, telecommunications and internet as follows:
I. GENERAL PROVISIONS


1.1 This Circular provides guidance for enterprises engaged in business activities in the domain of post and telecommunications and
Internet, as prescribed by law, which fall under the conditional business lines.
1.2 Post and/or telecommunications enterprises are enterprises engaged in business activities in one or several domains prescribed
in the Government�s Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP of November 12, 1997 on post and telecommunications. The conditional post and telecommunication
business lines include:
a/ Provision of postal and telecommunication services;
b/ Manufacture of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;


c/ Import, export, purchase and sale of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;
d/ Printing of postage stamps; production, import, export, purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage
stamps.
1.3 Internet services-providing enterprises are enterprises dealing in Internet services specified in the Government�s Decree No.
21/CP of March 5, 1997 issuing the Provisional Regulation on the management, establishment and use of the Internet in Vietnam".
The conditional Internet business lines include:
a/ Provision of Internet access services (IAP);
b/ Provision of Internet services (ISP).


1.4 The postal, telecommunication and Internet domains fall under the conditional business lines, where some business domains require
permits of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications while some others do not but must satisfy the conditions set in
this Circular.
1.5 Various kinds of permits and certificates used for technical and professional management prescribed in Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP
in order to ensure the network and service quality, ensure safety for operation of public and exclusive postal and telecommunication
networks and ensure the interests of users shall not be regulated by this Circular.


II. CONDITIONS FOR BUSINESS LINES WHICH REQUIRE PERMITS
2.1 The post, telecommunication and Internet business lines that require permits include:
a/ Establishment of national telecommunication backbone networks, public telecommunication networks and provision (direct or for resale)
of telecommunication services (basic, value-added);
b/ Establishment of Internet networks and provision of Internet services (IAP and ISP);
c/ Establishment of postal networks and provision of postal services;
d/ Printing of postage stamps;
e/ Manufacture of radio transmitters and receivers-transmitters.


2.2. Enterprises conducting business activities in the domains specified at Points a, b, c and d, Section 2.1 shall be State enterprises
or joint-stock companies where the State holds the predominant or special shares. For the domain specified at Point e, Section 2.1,
the business subjects shall be enterprises of any economic sector. Enterprises may do business in these domains under conditions
and according to the operating duration specified in their permits and start their business activities only when they obtain their
licenses.


2.3. Enterprises must make business registration according to law provisions before carrying out procedures applying for permits to
do business in the domains specified at Point 2.1 above.
2.4. The conditions, order and procedures for granting of permits to do business in the domains specified at Point 2.1 above shall
be as follows:
a/ For permits stated at Point a , the provisions in Circular No. 04/1998/TT-TCBD of September 29, 1998 of the General Department
of Post and Telecommunications guiding the Government�s Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP of November 12, 1997 on telecommunication networks
and services, shall be complied with.


b/ For permits specified at Point b, the provisions of Joint Circular No. 08/TTLT of May 24, 197 of the General Department of Post
and Telecommunications, the Ministry of the Interior (now the Ministry of Public Security) and the Ministry of Culture and Information
guiding the licensing of the connection, provision and use of Internet in Vietnam, shall be complied with;


c/ For permits specified at Point c, the provisions of Circular No. 02/1998/TT-TCBD of June 20, 1998 of the General Department of
Post and Telecommunications guiding the implementation of the Government�s Decree No. 109/1997/ND-CP on postal networks and services,
shall be complied with;
d/ For permits specified at Point d, the provisions of Decision No. 217/2000/QD-TCBD of March 6, 2000 of the General Department of
Post and Telecommunications issuing the Regulation on the professional management of postage stamps, shall be complied with.


e/ The order and procedures for licensing the manufacture of radio transmitters and/or receivers-transmitters:
- A dossier of application for permit shall consist of:
+ An application;
+ The enterprise�s organization and operation charter;
+ The production scheme with the following principal contents: category of equipment, technical properties (frequency, frequency band,
transmitting capacity of equipment�), technology and capacity of the production lines�


- Time limit for handling dossiers: The General Department of Post and Telecommunications shall evaluate and grant permits within
45 days after the receipt of valid dossiers. If there arise any matters which need to be re-examined, the above time-limit may be
extended but shall not exceed 60 days after receipt of valid dossiers. In case of refusal, the General Department of Post and Telecommunications
shall send written reply to the enterprise within the above time-limit.
III. CONDITIONS FOR BUSINESS LINES WHICH REQUIRE NO PERMIT
3.1 The conditional postal and telecommunication business lines which require no permit:


a/ Manufacture of post and telecommunication supplies and equipment (excluding radio transmitters and receivers-transmitters);
b/ Import and export of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;
c/ Purchase and sale of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment;
d/ Postal and telecommunication service provision agency;
e/ Agency for foreign express mail service companies;
f/ Import, export, purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage stamps.


3.2. Enterprises of all economic sectors that legally operate in Vietnam may register and do business in the domains specified at
Point 3.1 and shall be entitled to do business in such domains from the time they satisfy all business conditions set in this Circular
and commit themselves to maintain these conditions throughout the process of business operation.
3.3. During the process of business operation, enterprises must comply with law provisions on the goods and services quality, regulations
on information and advertisement, regulations on settlement of compensation claims as well as other relevant law provisions.


3.4. Business conditions for the manufacture of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment:
a/ For supplies and equipment on the "List of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment subject to standard conformity
certification" issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications, enterprises shall have to carry out the standard
conformity certification procedures for such supplies and equipment before circulating them on the market.


The order, procedures and conditions for standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment
are prescribed in the Regulation on the standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment,
issued together with Decision No. 285/2000/QD-TCBD of March 29, 2000 of the General Director of Post and Telecommunications.
b/ For subscribed terminal devices, enterprises shall have to effect the goods labeling thereof according to Circular No. 03/2000/TT-TCBD
of July 26, 2000 of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications.


3.5. Business conditions for the import and export of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment:
a/ For supplies and equipment on the "List of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment subject to standard conformity
certification", issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications, enterprises shall have to carry out the standard
conformity certification procedures for such supplies and equipment before importing them.


The order, procedures and conditions for standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment
are prescribed in the Regulation on the standard conformity certification of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment,
issued together with Decision No. 285/2000/QD-TCBD of March 29, 2000 of the General Director of Post and Telecommunications.


b/ For foreign-made subscribed terminal devices which are imported for sale on the Vietnamese market, enterprises shall have to effect
the goods labeling thereof according to Circular No. 03/2000/TT-TCBD of July 26, 2000 of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications.


c/ For radio transmitters and receivers-transmitters, enterprises may import only those with a frequency or frequency band in line
with the planning on the allocation of the frequency spectrum to operations in Vietnam, issued together with the Prime Minister�s
Decision No. 85/1998/QD-TTg of April 16, 1998 approving Vietnam�s planning on the allocation of the frequency spectrum to operations
and other relevant regulations of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications;


d/ For fixed satellite transmitters, receiver-transmitters used in telecommunication operations and broadcasting operations, enterprises
shall have to request their customers wishing to use such equipment to apply for permits to use transmitters and radio frequencies,
issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications before carrying out import procedures;
e/ Enterprises shall have to notify customers of those kinds of radio transmitters, receiver-transmitters which require the Post and
Telecommunications General Department�s permits for use of radio transmitters and frequencies;


f/ The import and export of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment for security and defense purposes shall comply with
the regulations of the Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of Defense.
3.6. Business conditions for the purchase and sale of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment:


a/ For supplies and equipment on the "List of postal and telecommunication supplies and equipment subject to standard conformity
certification", issued by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications, enterprises may only deal in the purchase
and sale of supplies and equipment already certified for their standard conformity as prescribed;
b/ For subscribed terminal devices, enterprises shall have to effect the goods labeling thereof according to Circular No. 03/2000/TT-TCBD
of July 26, 2000 of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications;


c/ For the purchase and sale of radio transmitters, receiver-transmitters, enterprises shall have to notify customers of those kinds
of radio transmitters, receiver-transmitters which require the Post and Telecommunications General Department�s licenses for use
of radio transmitters and frequencies;
3.7. Conditions for acting as postal and telecommunication service provision agents:


a/ Enterprises wishing to act as postal and telecommunication service provision agents must sign agency contracts with postal and
telecommunication service-providing enterprises or telecommunication service-reselling enterprises (hereinafter called the principals
for short). The agency contracts must clearly state kinds of postal and telecommunication services the agents are permitted to provide,
the quality and charge of each kind of service and the commission rate enjoyed by the agents.


b/ Pledge is made to provide the right services with proper quality as stated in the agency contracts and to collect charges at the
rates applied by the principals to users.
c/ Places of postal and telecommunication service provision agents must be put up with the commercial names and logos of the principals;


d/ Postal and telecommunication service provision agents must comply with the rules on postal and telecommunication services issued
by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications and submit to the inspection and supervision by the General Department of
Post and Telecommunications as well as competent State management bodies in the provision of postal and telecommunication services.
3.8. Conditions for acting as agents for foreign express mail service companies:


a/ Only enterprises licensed by the General Department of Post and Telecommunications to provide international postal services may
act as service agents (hereinafter called as agents for short) for foreign express mail service companies;
b/ Enterprises may sign agency contracts with foreign express mail service companies within the scope of international postal services
already licensed;
c/ Foreign express mail service companies that sign agency contracts must be those licensed to lawfully operate in one of the countries
with which Vietnam has established international post relations;


d/ Agency activities for foreign express mail service companies must ensure the national sovereignty and security as well as the interests
of service users and comply with the provisions of Vietnamese laws on post, tax, customs, information security and mail safety;


e/ Enterprises acting as agents for foreign express mail service companies, on the basis of Vietnamese laws and agreements with foreign
express mail service companies, shall have to formulate framework agency contracts for uniform application within the whole enterprises
and register such model contracts with the General Department of Post and Telecommunications; print matters used in transactions
with service users must be expressed in Vietnamese and a foreign language.


f/ Enterprises acting as agents for foreign express mail companies shall have to announce and post up at the transaction places the
service charges, service quality norms and users� rights and obligations;
g/ Enterprises acting as agents for foreign express mail service companies shall apply the annual regular or irregular regime of reporting
on the results of agency activities at the request of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications.
3.9. Conditions for conducting business in the import, export, purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity
postage stamps:


a/ Only enterprises licensed to do business in mail service may conduct import and export of postage stamps, stamp publications and
commodity postage stamps;
b/ Enterprises that deal in the purchase and sale of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage stamps must sign agency
contracts with mail service-providing enterprises;


c/ It is forbidden to purchase, sell, import or export any kind of postage stamps, stamp publications and commodity postage stamps,
which the General Department of Post and Telecommunications have suspended from issuance, banned from circulation or which have unhealthy
contents, incite or sow hatred among nations, infringe upon the national sovereignty and run counter to the Vietnamese traditional
practices and laws.
IV. IMPLEMENTATION PROVISIONS
4.1. This Circular takes effect 15 days after its signing. All the previous provisions which are contrary to this Circular are now
annulled.


4.2. Units of the General Department of Post and Telecommunications shall, within the scope of their relevant powers and tasks, have
to explain, guide, inspect and supervise the implementation of this Circular.
4.3. Enterprises shall have to strictly abide by the provisions of this Circular. Any problems arising in the course of implementation
should be promptly reported by enterprises to the General Department of Post and Telecommunications for guidance or explanation.
General Director of Post and Telecommunications
MAI LIEM TRUC

## 一、核心概括

越南对数字签名认证服务机构实行**分类许可与登记管理制度**：提供公共数字签名认证服务须经许可（Article 8），提供专用数字签名认证服务须办理登记（Article 4），向机构服务商签发数字证书须另行办理程序（Article 10）。核心规范为第37/2009/TT-BTTTT号通知，配套第26/2007/ND-CP号法令及工贸部第25/2006/QD-BTM号决定。

## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 公共数字签名认证服务的许可制度

**法规出处**：越南《关于数字签名认证服务机构许可、登记与认可档案及程序的规定》（第37/2009/TT-BTTTT号通知）第8条【来源2】。

**深度解读**：该条专门规定"提供公共数字签名认证服务的许可程序"（Procedures for licensing provision of public digital signature certification services）。所谓"公共"服务，指向不特定公众提供数字证书签发与认证的服务形态，因其涉及面广、外部性强，立法采取**事前许可**（licensing）模式，而非单纯备案。这与专用服务形成层次化监管：公共服务门槛更高、审查更严，体现立法者对公众信赖利益的重点保护。

**重点提示**：许可属**前置程序**，未获许可不得对外提供公共服务；申请材料须按通知规定的档案清单准备，程序性瑕疵可能导致退回补正，影响业务上线时间表。

**实务指引**：拟进入公共服务市场的机构，应首先对照第8条梳理申请档案清单，确认技术设施、人员资质与安全保障方案是否达标；建议在正式提交前进行内部合规预审，并预留补正时间。常见误区是将"登记"误认为"许可"，导致在未取得许可的情况下对外营业。

### 2. 专用数字签名认证服务的登记制度

**法规出处**：同通知第4条【来源1】。

**深度解读**：第4条规定"专用数字签名认证服务机构的运营登记"（Registration of operation of institutional providers of specialized digital signature certification services）。与公共服务许可不同，专用服务面向特定范围主体（如内部系统、特定行业用户），外部性较弱，故采**登记制**。这一"许可—登记"二元结构是越南数字签名监管的基本框架，反映风险分级、宽严相济的立法意图。

**重点提示**：登记虽程序相对简便，但**不得逾越服务范围**——专用机构若实质向公众提供服务，可能被认定为规避许可义务。

**实务指引**：明确自身服务对象的封闭性，在登记材料中准确界定服务范围；建立用户准入机制以佐证"专用"属性；如业务扩展至公共服务领域，须另行申请许可，切勿以登记替代许可。

### 3. 向机构服务商签发数字证书的程序

**法规出处**：同通知第10条【来源4】。

**深度解读**：第10条规定"向公共数字签名认证服务机构签发数字证书的程序"（Procedures for issuance of digital certificates to institutional providers of public digital signature certification services）。这表明认证服务体系具有**层级结构**：机构服务商自身亦须从根认证机构体系获得数字证书，方能开展业务。该条与第8条许可程序衔接，构成"先许可、后发证"的完整链条。

**重点提示**：数字证书的签发以许可为前提，二者顺序不可颠倒；证书申请须使用规定格式。

**实务指引**：取得许可后应及时启动证书申请，避免"有证无照"无法实际运营；关注根认证机构网站公布的最新认证规则，确保申请材料与规则同步更新。

### 4. 申请档案的具体构成

**法规出处**：同通知第2条，援引第26/2007/ND-CP号法令第21条所列文件【来源5】。

**深度解读**：第2条明确数字证书申请档案包括：按通知附录V规定格式制作的**数字证书申请表**，以及根认证机构在网站（http://www.rootca.gov.vn）公布的**认证规则所要求的文件**。这一设计将部分材料要求"动态援引"至根认证机构规则，使档案要求可随技术标准更新而调整，兼顾稳定性与灵活性。

**重点提示**：申请表格式为**强制格式**（附录V），自制格式不予接受；认证规则文件须以根认证机构网站公布版本为准，注意版本时效。

**实务指引**：提交前逐项核对附录V格式与网站规则清单；建立材料版本管理台账，防止因规则更新导致材料过期；保留提交凭证以备程序查询。

### 5. 数字签名使用的内部规范

**法规出处**：越南工贸部《数字签名使用条例》（第25/2006/QD-BTM号决定）【来源3】。

**深度解读**：该决定附发的条例对工贸部系统内数字签名的使用作出规定，并明确办公厅、电子商务局负责人及工贸部干部公务员的实施义务。这体现"**机构先行、内部规范**"的推进路径：政府机关率先建立数字签名使用规则，为市场主体提供示范。

**重点提示**：该条例适用范围限于工贸部系统，不直接约束一般企业，但可作为企业设计内部数字签名管理制度的参考范本。

**实务指引**：企业与工贸部有业务往来时，应了解其数字签名使用要求以确保文件互认；内部制度建设可借鉴该条例的责任分工与实施机制。

## 三、总结与建议

越南对数字签名认证服务机构采取**"公共服务许可、专用服务登记、机构证书另发"**的三层监管架构，核心依据为第37/2009/TT-BTTTT号通知第4、8、10条及第2条档案规定，配套第26/2007/ND-CP号法令与工贸部第25/2006/QD-BTM号决定。行动上，应先界定服务性质（公共或专用），据此选择许可或登记路径，再依第2条及根认证机构规则备齐档案。

延伸提醒：其一，密切跟踪根认证机构网站规则更新，材料要求可能动态调整；其二，服务范围变化须及时办理相应许可或变更，避免超范围经营；其三，涉及与越南政府机关的数字签名互认时，注意其内部使用规范的特殊要求。

## 一、核心概括

亚洲各法域个人资料保护立法呈现"原则共通、路径分化"格局。马来西亚与新加坡均以**七项/多项保护原则**为核心框架，但新加坡对"个人资料""组织""处理"等基础概念作出详尽立法定义，马来西亚则以原则列举加数据主体权利（查阅、更正、阻止处理）为骨架；澳门则通过《个人资料保护法》作为通用法，在行业立法中援引适用。三地共同点是承认数据主体的查阅、更正与反对处理权，差异在于立法精细度、适用范围及跨境/公共部门数据处理规则。

## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 马来西亚：以"保护原则"为核心的框架

**法规出处**：马来西亚《Personal Data Protection Act 2010》第5条【来源1】。

**深度解读**：该条以目录式列举方式确立七项原则——**一般原则、通知与选择原则、披露原则、安全原则、保留原则、数据完整性原则、查阅原则**。这一结构表明马来西亚采取"原则导向"立法，将资料处理全生命周期（收集、通知、披露、保管、保留、更正、查阅）拆解为可独立适用的义务模块。其立法意图在于以原则覆盖商业交易中的资料处理行为，而非逐项规定技术细节，因而赋予数据使用者一定合规弹性，但也要求其自行建立对应内部政策。

**重点提示**：七项原则并非并列宣示，而是相互衔接——通知与选择原则是收集阶段的前置义务，披露原则约束对外提供，安全与保留原则约束存储，查阅原则保障数据主体事后权利。违反任一原则均可能构成违法，合规审查需逐项对照。

**实务指引**：企业应建立"原则对照表"，将七项原则映射至内部流程（收集表单、隐私通知、第三方共享协议、安全措施、保留期限表、更正机制、查阅响应流程）。常见误区是仅准备隐私政策文本而忽视保留期限与安全措施的落地记录。

### 2. 马来西亚：数据主体的查阅与更正权

**法规出处**：马来西亚《Personal Data Protection Act 2010》第12条【来源1】【知识图谱关联】。

**深度解读**：该条明确数据主体有权**查阅**其被持有的个人资料，并在资料**不准确、不完整、具误导性或非最新**时要求**更正**，但法律另有拒绝事由的除外。这构成数据主体权利的核心救济机制，与第5条"查阅原则"形成呼应。知识图谱关联进一步显示，数据主体还可依据第42条发出书面通知，要求数据使用者**停止或不得开始**特定目的或方式的处理，即"阻止处理权"。

**重点提示**：查阅与更正权的行使受法定拒绝情形限制，企业需在响应时限与拒绝理由上留存书面依据。第42条的"数据主体通知"须以**书面**形式作出，并给予合理期限，程序性要求不可省略。

**实务指引**：建议建立标准化的查阅/更正申请受理流程，记录申请时间、身份核验、响应结果及拒绝理由；对第42条通知应设置内部升级机制，避免逾期未处理引发争议。

### 3. 新加坡：以"定义先行"构建适用范围

**法规出处**：新加坡《Personal Data Protection Act 2012》第2条【来源3】。

**深度解读**：新加坡第2条以大量立法定义界定适用范围，关键包括：**"个人资料"**指可从不该项资料或结合组织可获取的其他信息识别个人的资料（无论真实与否）；**"组织"**涵盖个人、公司、社团，且**不论是否在新加坡设立或注册、是否驻留或设有营业地**；**"处理"**包括记录、持有、组织、改编、检索、组合、传输、删除或销毁。这种"定义先行"模式使法律适用边界清晰，尤其"组织"的域外延展意味着境外主体处理新加坡境内相关资料也可能受辖。

**重点提示**：定义中区分了**"数据中介"**（代他组织处理而不为自身目的处理）与数据使用者，前者义务配置不同；**"商业联系方式"**与**"公开可得资料"**等概念设有特定处理规则，需在合规分类时单独识别。

**实务指引**：企业应先完成"资料地图"，按定义判断自身是组织还是数据中介、资料是否属个人资料、处理活动是否落入例外（如个人/家庭目的）。常见误区是误以为境外主体不受辖，或混淆数据中介与数据使用者的义务。

### 4. 澳门：通用法加行业援引的适用模式

**法规出处**：中国澳门第8/2005号法律《个人资料保护法》，经《非强制性中央公积金制度》【来源2】、《会计师专业及执业资格制度》【来源4】、《电子政务》【来源5】等法规援引适用。

**深度解读**：澳门并未在行业立法中另设一套资料保护规则，而是以第8/2005号法律为**通用法**，由各单行法规以"根据第8/2005号法律的规定"方式援引。例如社保基金处理央积金行政程序时，可与公共实体及基金管理实体进行**资料互联、提供、互换、确认及使用**【来源2】；会计师委员会同样可采取包括资料互联在内的方式与公共实体交换资料【来源4】；电子政务领域则明确公共部门执行资料操作（含比较和互联）须**尊重自然人权利或受法律保护的利益**，并按第8/2005号法律进行【来源5】。

**重点提示**：该模式的特点是"通用规则统一、行业场景细化"。资料互联并非无限制授权，仍须回归第8/2005号法律的合法性、目的限制与权利保障要求。电子政务条文特别强调权利与利益的尊重，提示公共部门互联操作需有法律依据与必要性支撑。

**实务指引**：在澳门开展涉及资料互联的项目，应先确认单行法规是否提供援引依据，再依第8/2005号法律评估处理的合法性基础、目的正当性及数据主体权利保障措施，并留存互联必要性的说明文件。

### 5. 三法域的共同点与差异点

**深度解读**：共同点在于三地均承认**数据主体的查阅、更正与反对/阻止处理权**（马来西亚第12条、第42条；新加坡以定义与义务体系支撑；澳门回归第8/2005号法律的权利保障），且均以"目的限制"为合规基石。差异点在于：马来西亚采**原则列举式**，结构清晰但概念定义相对简略；新加坡采**定义密集型**，适用范围与主体分类精细，域外效力明确；澳门采**通用法加行业援引**，规则统一但分散于各单行法规，需逐行业检索适用依据。

**重点提示**：跨法域经营时，不能以单一法域的"原则清单"直接套用，须分别核对主体定义、适用范围与例外。

**实务指引**：建议制作三地对照合规矩阵，按"资料定义—主体分类—处理义务—数据主体权利—跨境/互联规则"五栏逐项比对，识别最严标准并统一内部政策。

## 三、总结与建议

| 比较维度 | 马来西亚 | 新加坡 | 澳门 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 立法结构 | 七项保护原则【来源1】 | 定义先行+义务体系【来源3】 | 通用法+行业援引【来源2】【来源4】【来源5】 |
| 适用范围 | 商业交易中的资料处理 | 组织定义含域外延展 | 依单行法规场景确定 |
| 数据主体权利 | 查阅、更正、阻止处理【来源1】 | 以义务体系保障 | 回归第8/2005号法律 |
| 严格程度 | 原则导向，弹性较大 | 定义精细，适用边界严 | 统一规则，行业细化 |

**总结**：三地共同承认查阅、更正与反对处理权，差异主要在立法技术与适用范围界定。马来西亚以原则清单便于对照，新加坡以定义精确划定边界，澳门以通用法加援引实现统一。行动上，企业应按法域分别完成资料地图与合规矩阵，重点核查主体定义、例外情形与资料互联依据。

**延伸提醒**：其一，新加坡"组织"定义的域外效力可能使境外主体受辖，跨境业务需提前评估；其二，澳门资料互联须有单行法规援引依据，不可仅凭通用法推定授权；其三，马来西亚第42条书面通知程序不可简化，逾期处理存在合规风险。

## 一、核心概括

现有法规资料仅涵盖美国反洗钱合规制度（31 CFR Chapter X），**未提供亚太各国FATF标准执行情况的具体法规或评估数据**。以下基于美国各行业反洗钱合规要求，提炼FATF核心义务的落地范式，供理解亚太各国合规框架时作比较参照。

## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 反洗钱方案的法定化与监管审批要求

**法规出处**：美国《Rules for Mutual Funds》1024.210(a)；《Rules for Banks》1020.210(a)【来源1】【来源2】

**深度解读**：美国将FATF“风险为本”原则转化为强制性的书面合规方案要求。共同基金须制定**书面反洗钱方案**，并经董事会书面批准，供SEC检查【来源1】；受联邦功能监管的银行实施并维持合规方案即视为满足《银行保密法》31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1)的要求【来源2】。立法意图在于将反洗钱从原则性倡导升级为**可审查、可问责**的法定义务，监管机构据此获得检查与执法抓手。

**重点提示**：方案须“合理设计”以预防洗钱及恐怖融资，而非形式合规；董事会批准是治理层面的硬性要求，缺失即构成违规。

**实务指引**：金融机构应准备：①书面方案文本；②董事会/高级管理层批准决议；③方案可供监管检查的存档机制。常见误区是将方案制定视为一次性工作，忽视持续更新义务。

### 2. 五项核心要素的标准化配置

**法规出处**：《Rules for Banks》1020.210(a)(2)(i)-(v)【来源2】

**深度解读**：美国将FATF建议的核心要素固化为五项最低要求：**内部控制体系、独立测试、合规负责人指定、人员培训、风险为本的客户尽职调查**。其中客户尽职调查明确要求理解客户关系的性质与目的以建立风险画像，并持续监测可疑交易、按风险维护更新客户信息，且客户信息须包含法人客户**受益所有人**信息【来源2】。这一结构与FATF建议10（CDD）、建议15（新技术）、建议18（内部控制）高度对应，是评估各国执行力的通用标尺。

**重点提示**：独立测试可由内部人员或外部第三方执行，但测试人不得同时是合规方案运营人；受益所有人信息收集是2016年后强化重点。

**实务指引**：建议按“五要素清单”逐项自查，尤其关注CDD中受益所有人识别的完整性，以及独立测试的独立性证据留存。

### 3. 行业差异化与风险为本的灵活适用

**法规出处**：《Rules for Real Estate》1029.210(b)(1)；《Rules for Casinos》1027.210(b)(1)【来源3】【来源4】

**深度解读**：不同行业的反洗钱方案须基于**自身产品服务的风险评估**设计内控。贷款金融公司须将**代理人和经纪人纳入方案**，并获取有效反洗钱所需全部客户信息【来源3】；贵金属珠宝经销商须综合考量产品类型、客户与供应链性质、分销渠道、地理区位，以及是否涉及被认定为支持国际恐怖主义或反洗钱不合作司法辖区的交易【来源4】。这体现FATF“风险为本”方法在行业层面的差异化落地。

**重点提示**：风险自评估是方案设计的起点，监管检查首先审视评估是否覆盖全部相关因素；高风险情形（如大额现金、第三方付款、异常保密要求）须有识别与拒绝交易的程序【来源4】。

**实务指引**：企业应建立**书面风险自评估报告**，列明产品、客户、渠道、地域四维度风险，并据此配置内控强度；代理商管理须有培训与合规验证记录。

### 4. 合规负责人制度与独立测试机制

**法规出处**：《Rules for Dealers in Precious Metals》1028.210(b)(2)、(b)(4)【来源5】

**深度解读**：合规负责人须确保方案有效实施、按风险因素与监管要求变化及时更新、并组织人员培训【来源5】。独立审计的范围与频率须与风险相称，可由内部人员执行，但**不得为合规负责人或方案运营参与者**【来源5】。该设计确保“执行”与“监督”职能分离，是FATF建议18内部控制的典型制度表达。

**重点提示**：合规负责人缺位或兼任测试人，将直接削弱方案的可信度；审计频率须有风险评估支撑。

**实务指引**：明确任命合规负责人并以书面文件固定职责；独立测试报告应留存备查，测试发现的问题须有整改闭环记录。

### 5. 方案的可获取性与执法后果

**法规出处**：《Rules for Loan or Finance Companies》1029.210(a)、(c)【来源3】

**深度解读**：方案须应FinCEN或其指定机构要求提供副本；不遵守该节要求可能构成对《银行保密法》及该部分的违反，由FinCEN或其授权机构检查【来源3】。这表明合规方案不仅是内部文件，更是**监管可随时调取的执法证据**，违规面临BSA项下的法律后果。

**重点提示**：方案须保持“随时可提交”状态，过期版本或缺失更新记录均构成风险。

**实务指引**：建立方案版本管理与归档制度，确保监管问询时能即时提供最新有效文本及批准、测试、培训记录。

## 三、总结与建议

现有资料仅覆盖美国反洗钱合规框架，**无法据此评价亚太各国FATF标准执行表现**。但美国制度提供了可迁移的评估维度：书面方案与治理层批准、五要素最低配置、行业风险自评估、合规负责人与独立测试分离、监管可获取性。建议在评估亚太各国时，以FATF互评估报告及各国具体法规为准，重点核查：①CDD中受益所有人识别是否落地；②独立测试的独立性；③风险为本方法在行业规则中的体现。延伸提醒：FATF标准为最低要求，各国执行宽严不一，须以当地有效法规和监管指引为最终依据；跨境业务应同时评估母国与东道国双重合规义务。

## 一、核心概括

亚太各法域对FinTech的监管路径差异显著：新加坡以统一立法框架覆盖数字代币服务商等新型主体，美国侧重跨境账户申报与反洗钱合规，中国大陆聚焦汽车金融公司等细分机构的信息科技风险管控，泰国则以反洗钱法界定金融科技相关交易的可疑标准。以下基于现有法规资料逐一解读。

## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 新加坡：以统一金融立法覆盖数字代币服务商

**法规出处**：新加坡《Financial Services and Markets Act 2022》第2条（定义条款）【来源1】。

**深度解读**：该法开篇即对"金融机构"作出极为宽泛的列举式定义，涵盖银行、商人银行、金融公司、支付服务持牌人、保险机构、资本市场服务持牌人、信托公司、指定金融控股公司，以及**依据本法获牌从事数字代币服务业务的主体**（第2条(q)项）【来源1】。立法意图在于将FinTech领域中最具代表性的数字代币服务纳入统一监管框架，避免碎片化立法带来的监管套利。值得注意的是，该定义还通过(q)项兜底条款，将依本法或任何"MAS附表法案"获许可、批准、授权、指定、认可、登记或受监管的主体一并纳入，同时明确排除依《证券与期货法》第286条授权或第287条认可的集合投资计划【来源1】。

**重点提示**：该法采取分阶段生效模式，不同部分分别于2022年6月30日、2023年4月28日、2024年5月10日、2024年7月31日及2025年6月30日陆续生效【来源1】。数字代币服务提供商的牌照要求及具体合规义务，需结合对应部分的生效时间判断适用节点。

**实务指引**：拟在新加坡开展数字代币服务的企业，应首先对照第2条(q)项确认自身是否落入"金融机构"定义范围；其次核查拟开展业务对应的法案部分是否已生效；再次准备牌照申请材料时，需同时关注MAS附表法案下的交叉监管要求。常见误区是仅关注《支付服务法》而忽略本法对数字代币服务商的独立牌照要求。

### 2. 美国：跨境金融账户申报制度对FinTech账户的覆盖

**法规出处**：美国《Bank Secrecy Act Regulations》31 CFR 1010.350【来源2】。

**深度解读**：该条要求"美国人士"对在外国拥有金融利益或签字权/其他权限的银行、证券及其他金融账户，须每年向国税局局长申报（FBAR表格）【来源2】。就FinTech而言，第(c)(3)条对"其他金融账户"的定义尤为关键：包括存款类金融机构账户、具有现金价值的保险或年金保单、期货期权经纪商账户，以及**向公众发行份额、定期确定净值并可定期赎回的共同基金或类似集合基金账户**【来源2】。这意味着FinTech平台上的投资账户、数字资产托管账户（如符合上述特征）可能触发申报义务。第(e)条对"金融利益"的界定涵盖记录所有人、法律所有权人，以及通过代理人、 nominee、持股超50%的实体、信托等间接持有的情形，并设有反规避条款【来源2】。

**重点提示**：第(g)(1)和(g)(2)条规定，拥有金融利益或签字权的境外金融账户达**25个及以上**时，可仅申报账户数量及基本信息，但税务机关有权要求补充明细【来源2】。第(f)(2)条列明了银行、受SEC/CFTC监管金融机构、授权服务提供商及上市公司等主体的高管或雇员的签字权申报豁免情形【来源2】。

**实务指引**：FinTech企业若涉及美国人士客户或自身为美国人士，应建立账户属性识别机制，判断是否构成"其他金融账户"；对超过25个账户的情形善用简化申报规则；同时注意第(e)(2)(3)条反规避规则，避免通过设立实体规避申报。常见误区是将纯支付账户一概排除，但若该账户具有存款或投资特征，仍可能落入申报范围。

### 3. 中国大陆：汽车金融公司的信息科技风险管理要求

**法规出处**：中国大陆《汽车金融公司管理办法》第47条【来源3】。

**深度解读**：该条要求汽车金融公司建立**与信息系统运行管理模式相匹配的信息科技风险管理体系**，强化网络安全、数据安全、业务连续性、外包等领域的风险防控，保障信息系统安全稳定运行【来源3】。虽然条文本身未直接使用"FinTech"表述，但其规范对象——汽车金融公司——正是金融科技应用密集的细分领域（如线上信贷审批、车联网数据风控、外包科技服务等）。立法意图在于将信息科技风险纳入机构全面风险管理框架，强调"匹配性"原则，即风控体系须与机构自身的信息系统运行管理模式相适应，而非一刀切。

**重点提示**：该条明确列举了**网络安全、数据安全、业务连续性、外包**四大重点领域，机构在这四个方面的制度建设将成为监管检查的重点。特别是外包领域，FinTech机构普遍依赖第三方科技服务商，外包风险管理不到位可能直接构成违规。

**实务指引**：汽车金融公司应：第一，梳理信息系统运行管理模式，形成与风控体系的匹配性说明文档；第二，针对四大领域分别制定专项制度并定期演练（尤其是业务连续性预案）；第三，建立外包服务商准入、监控和退出机制。常见误区是将信息科技风险等同于IT部门职责，忽视董事会和高管层的最终责任。

### 4. 泰国：反洗钱法对金融科技交易的"可疑交易"界定

**法规出处**：泰国《Money Laundering Control Act, 1999》第3条（定义条款）【来源4】。

**深度解读**：该条对"交易""可疑交易""与犯罪有关的财产""金融机构"等核心概念作出界定【来源4】。"可疑交易"包括：与同类交易相比**性质异常复杂**的交易、**缺乏经济可行性**的交易、**合理相信为规避本法适用**而进行的交易，以及与上游犯罪有关或可能有关的交易，不论次数多寡【来源4】。"金融机构"的定义涵盖泰国银行、商业银行、金融公司、证券公司、人寿及非人寿保险公司、储蓄合作社，以及**部长级法规规定的其他与金融相关业务的法律实体**【来源4】。这一兜底条款为将FinTech业务纳入反洗钱监管预留了空间。上游犯罪清单涵盖毒品、性犯罪、公共欺诈、侵占诈骗、渎职、敲诈勒索、走私等【来源4】。

**重点提示**：可疑交易的判断标准不依赖交易金额门槛，而侧重交易性质、经济合理性和规避意图，这对FinTech平台的高频、小额、跨境交易模式构成特殊挑战。金融机构须履行可疑交易报告义务，具体程序性要求需结合本法其他条款。

**实务指引**：在泰运营的FinTech机构应建立交易监测规则，重点关注：结构异常复杂的交易链路、缺乏商业合理性的资金流动、疑似拆分规避报告的行为。同时应持续关注部长级法规是否将自身业务类型纳入"金融机构"定义。常见误区是仅以金额阈值作为监测标准，忽视定性判断维度。

### 5. 中国大陆：银行保险机构许可证管理的特许经营框架

**法规出处**：中国大陆《银行保险机构许可证管理办法》第2条【来源5】。

**深度解读**：该条明确许可证是国家金融监督管理总局依法颁发的**特许银行保险机构经营金融业务的法律文件**，其颁发、换发、收缴等由金融监管总局及其授权派出机构依法行使，**其他任何单位和个人不得行使上述职权**【来源5】。这一规定确立了FinTech涉足银行保险业务的特许经营底线：任何主体从事需持牌的银行保险业务，必须经法定程序取得许可证，科技公司不得以"科技赋能"名义实质经营持牌业务。

**重点提示**：条文强调许可证职权的**专属性**，排除了地方政府、行业协会或其他机构颁发类似资质文件的可能性。对于与银行保险机构合作的FinTech企业，需注意合作模式不得构成无证经营或变相出借牌照。

**实务指引**：FinTech企业涉足银行保险业务前，应进行牌照映射分析，明确自身业务是否落入特许范围；与持牌机构合作时，应在协议中明确双方角色边界，避免实质承担持牌业务职能。常见误区是以"技术服务"包装实质持牌业务，构成无证经营风险。

## 三、总结与建议

**多法域对比简表**：

| 法域 | 监管模式 | 核心特征 | 严格程度 |
|------|----------|----------|----------|
| 新加坡 | 统一立法+分阶段生效 | 数字代币服务商纳入"金融机构"定义，牌照覆盖 | 高（专门立法） |
| 美国 | 申报制+反洗钱 | 跨境账户申报，25账户简化规则 | 中高（申报义务明确） |
| 中国大陆 | 分业特许+专项风控 | 汽车金融公司信息科技风控；许可证专属职权 | 中（分领域规范） |
| 泰国 | 反洗钱定义扩张 | 可疑交易定性标准，金融机构兜底定义 | 中（依赖部长级法规） |

**主要差异**：新加坡采取**事前牌照准入**的统一立法模式；美国侧重**事后申报与信息透明**；中国大陆以**分业特许经营**为基础，辅以专项信息科技风控要求；泰国则通过**反洗钱定义条款**间接覆盖FinTech业务。共同点在于均强调对新型金融主体的穿透式识别和风险防控。

**行动指引**：企业进入亚太市场前，应逐法域进行监管映射，重点识别是否触发牌照、申报或报告义务；建立跨法域的合规监测机制，关注分阶段生效和部长级法规的动态变化。

**延伸提醒**：第一，新加坡法的分阶段生效意味着合规义务随时间递增，需持续跟踪；第二，美国FBAR的"金融利益"认定含反规避规则，架构设计需审慎；第三，泰国可疑交易标准为定性判断，FinTech高频交易模式下的监测系统需专门调校。

An Act to provide for a financial sector-wide regulation of financial services and markets, the exercise of control over and the resolution of financial institutions and their related entities, the licensing and regulation of digital token service providers, and other incidental and connected matters, to make related and consequential amendments to certain other Acts, and to amend a provision of the Income Tax Act 1947 consequent upon the operation of the Financial Holding Companies Act 2013.
Be it enacted by the President with the advice and consent of the Parliament of Singapore, as follows:
PART 1
PRELIMINARYShort title and commencement


This Act is the Financial Services and Markets Act 2022 and comes into operation on a date that the Minister appoints by notification in the
Gazette
.
InterpretationIn this Act, unless the context otherwise requires —

“bank” means a bank licensed under the Banking Act 1970;
“corporation” has the meaning given by section 4(1) of the Companies Act 1967;
“financial institution” means —

(a)
any bank;
(b)
any merchant bank licensed under the Banking Act 1970;
(c)
any finance company licensed under the Finance Companies Act 1967;
(d)
any person that is approved as a financial institution under section 4;
(e)
a person granted a licence under the Payment Services Act 2019;
(f)
any insurer licensed or regulated under the Insurance Act 1966;
(g)
any insurance intermediary registered or regulated under the Insurance Act 1966;
(h)
any financial adviser licensed under the Financial Advisers Act 2001;


(i)
any approved holding company, approved exchange, recognised market operator, licensed trade repository, licensed foreign trade repository, approved clearing house, recognised clearing house, authorised benchmark administrator, authorised benchmark submitter, designated benchmark submitter or holder of a capital markets services licence under the Securities and Futures Act 2001;
(j)
any trustee for a collective investment scheme authorised under section 286 of the Securities and Futures Act 2001, that is approved under that Act;

(p)

In general.

31 U.S.C. 5314
to be filed by such persons. The form prescribed under section 5314 is the Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (TD-F 90-22.1), or any successor form.

and

(b)
United States person.

(1)
A citizen of the United States;
(2)

(c)
Types of reportable accounts.
For purposes of this section—
(1)
Bank account.
The term “bank account” means a savings deposit, demand deposit, checking, or any other account maintained with a person engaged in the business of banking.


(2)
Securities account.
The term “securities account” means an account with a person engaged in the business of buying, selling, holding or trading stock or other securities.
(3)
Other financial account.
The term “other financial account” means—
(i)
An account with a person that is in the business of accepting deposits as a financial agency;
(
ii
)
An account that is an insurance or annuity policy with a cash value;
(
iii
)
An account with a person that acts as a broker or dealer for futures or options transactions in any commodity on or subject to the rules of a commodity exchange or association; or

iv

An account with—

Mutual fund or similar pooled fund.

Other investment fund.

Exceptions for certain accounts.

 For this purpose, an entity generally exercises governmental authority on behalf of the United States, an Indian Tribe, a State, or a political subdivision only if its authorities include one or more of the powers to tax, to exercise the power of eminent domain, or to exercise police powers with respect to matters within its jurisdiction.

Anti-avoidance rule.
A United States person that causes an entity, including but not limited to a corporation, partnership, or trust, to be created for a purpose of evading this section shall have a financial interest in any bank, securities, or other financial account in a foreign country for which the entity is the owner of record or holder of legal title.

Signature or other authority
—(1)
In general.
Signature or other authority means the authority of an individual (alone or in conjunction with another) to control the disposition of money, funds or other assets held in a financial account by direct communication (whether in writing or otherwise) to the person with whom the financial account is maintained.

(2)
Exceptions

ii

iii

iv

(v)

Special rules
—(1)

A United States person having a financial interest in 25 or more foreign financial accounts need only provide the number of financial accounts and certain other basic information on the report, but will be required to provide detailed information concerning each account when so requested by the Secretary or his delegate.


(2)
Signature or other authority over 25 or more foreign financial accounts.
A United States person having signature or other authority over 25 or more foreign financial accounts need only provide the number of financial accounts and certain other basic information on the report, but will be required to provide detailed information concerning each account when so requested by the Secretary or his delegate.

Consolidated reports.

## 一、核心概括（80-100字）

基于现有资料，仅美国联邦层面法规有明确数据泄露通知规定，亚太各国（地区）具体规则资料暂未提供。美国体系下，HIPAA覆盖实体须在发现泄露后**60日内**通知个人，触发条件为"发现"非授权获取；FTC健康记录规则同样设60日框架但增加FTC与媒体通知义务。亚太地区差异需另行查证。

## 二、法律依据详解

### 1. 触发条件的核心标准："发现"时点而非"发生"时点

**法规出处**：美国《HIPAA - Security and Privacy》164.404(a)(2)【来源1】；《Exemption for Affiliates from Fair Credit Reporting Act》318.3(c)【来源2】；164.410(a)(2)【来源3】。

**深度解读**：三部法规均将"发现"（discovery）作为通知义务的起算点，而非泄露实际发生日。HIPAA将"发现"定义为：泄露首次被覆盖实体知悉之日，或通过**合理勤勉**应当知悉之日。更关键的是，法规采用**归责推定**——只要泄露被任何员工、高管或代理人（除实施泄露者本人）知悉，即视为该实体已知悉。这一推定的立法意图在于防止企业以"管理层不知情"为由拖延通知。FTC规则318.3(c)采用相同逻辑，将员工或代理人的知悉归于vendor或PHR相关实体。

**重点提示**：合理勤勉标准意味着企业不能被动等待泄露被上报，而应建立主动监测机制。若IT人员发现异常但未上报管理层，法律上仍视为企业"已发现"，60日时钟即已启动。

**实务指引**：建立内部**泄露发现即时上报制度**，明确任何员工发现疑似泄露须在24小时内上报合规负责人；保留发现时间戳记录（如日志、邮件），以证明60日起算点；对第三方服务商（business associate）的知悉同样归责于本企业，须在合同中约定其即时通报义务。

### 2. 通知时限：60日上限与"无不合理延迟"双重约束

**法规出处**：HIPAA 164.404(b)【来源1】；164.410(b)【来源3】；164.406(b)【来源4】；FTC规则318.3(a)【来源2】。

**深度解读**：HIPAA对个人通知、媒体通知、商业伙伴向覆盖实体通知均设定**"无不合理延迟，且不超过发现后60个日历日"**的双重标准。这意味着60日并非"安全港"——即使未满60日，若延迟缺乏合理理由仍构成违规。FTC规则318.3(a)对PHR vendor的通知义务援引318.4至318.6，时限框架与HIPAA类似，但增加了向FTC和媒体通报的独立义务（500人以上居民受影响时）。

**重点提示**：60日为**日历日**而非工作日；法规允许"分批通知"（one or more mailings as information is available），即信息不完整时可先发初步通知再补充，但首次通知仍须在60日内发出。

**实务指引**：制定**60日倒计时应急预案**，发现泄露后立即启动；若调查未完成，先发出含已知信息的初步通知，后续补充；对商业伙伴（business associate）合同约定其须在发现后**30日内**通知覆盖实体，为后者留出向个人通知的缓冲期。

### 3. 通知内容与方式的法定要素

**法规出处**：HIPAA 164.404(c)(1)(A)-(E)【来源1】；164.404(d)(1)-(3)【来源1】；164.410(c)【来源3】。

**深度解读**：个人通知须包含五项要素：泄露描述（含发生日与发现日）、涉及信息类型、个人应采取的保护措施、实体正在采取的调查与缓解措施、联系方式（含免费电话）。通知须以**通俗语言**（plain language）书写。方式上首选**一类邮件**寄送至最后已知地址；若个人同意且未撤回，可用电子邮件。特殊情形：已知个人死亡时通知近亲属或遗产代理人；联系信息不足时，少于10人可用替代书面通知或电话，10人以上须在网站显著位置张贴90日或通过主要媒体公告，并设至少90日有效的免费电话。

**重点提示**：商业伙伴（business associate）向覆盖实体的通知须包含**每个受影响个人的身份识别**，并提供覆盖实体向个人通知所需的全部信息【来源3】。

**实务指引**：预先起草**通知模板**，确保涵盖五项法定要素并用通俗语言；建立地址核验流程以减少"联系信息不足"情形；网站张贴替代通知时保留90日截图证据；商业伙伴合同中明确其通知须包含个人身份清单。

### 4. 媒体通知与监管通知的附加触发门槛

**法规出处**：HIPAA 164.406(a)【来源4】；FTC规则318.3(a)(2)-(3)【来源2】；《Standards for Safeguarding Customer Information》314.4(j)【来源5】。

**深度解读**：HIPAA要求，当泄露涉及**超过500名**某州或司法管辖区居民时，须通知该州主要媒体，时限同样为60日【来源4】。FTC规则对PHR vendor设定类似门槛：500名以上居民受影响时须通知主要媒体和FTC【来源2】。此外，FTC《客户信息保护标准》314.4(j)要求金融机构在涉及**至少500名消费者**的通知事件中发现后**30日内**电子通知FTC，且执法官员可请求初始延迟30日、再延长60日【来源5】。可见美国体系呈现"个人通知60日、监管通知30日"的差异化时限结构。

**重点提示**：媒体通知的内容须满足与个人通知相同的要素要求【来源4(c)】；FTC通知须通过其网站在线表单提交，含事件描述、信息类型、受影响人数等六项内容【来源5(j)(1)】。

**实务指引**：建立**受影响人数快速统计机制**，以判断是否触发500人门槛；对金融机构而言，FTC通知的30日时限短于个人通知，须优先处理；与执法机构沟通延迟通知时，取得书面认定并保留记录。

### 5. 亚太地区规定的资料缺口说明

**法规出处**：现有资料中仅【知识图谱关联】提及日本《Act on the Protection of Personal Information》第84条、第85条及台湾地区《個人資料保護法》第21条涉及"通知义务"，但图谱摘录仅显示第84条关于披露决定期限的例外，**未提供泄露通知的具体时限与触发条件条文**。

**深度解读**：知识图谱关联仅能佐证上述法域存在通知义务的实体关系，但其权威性低于具体法条，且摘录内容不涉及泄露通知的时限或触发标准。因此，**关于亚太各国数据泄露通知义务在时限和触发条件上的具体异同，现有法规资料暂未提供明确规定**，无法据此作出可靠比较。

**重点提示**：不得依据图谱关联推断日本或台湾地区的具体时限数字；如需亚太比较，须补充检索各国个人数据保护法的泄露通知专条。

**实务指引**：若企业业务覆盖亚太，建议另行委托当地律师就日本《个人情報保護法》第26条、新加坡PDPA、澳大利亚NDB scheme等专项核查；在资料补齐前，对亚太法域采取**保守合规策略**，参照美国60日标准作为内部上限。

## 三、总结与建议（150-200字）

现有资料仅支持美国联邦层面的结论：HIPAA体系以"发现"为起算点，个人与媒体通知上限**60日**，FTC监管通知为**30日**（金融机构），触发门槛分别为非授权获取和500人规模。亚太各国具体规则资料暂缺，无法完成比较。建议：一是对美国业务建立60日倒计时与30日FTC通报双轨机制；二是对亚太业务另行检索当地泄露通知专条后再定合规方案；三是切勿以知识图谱关联替代具体法条作为合规依据。延伸提醒：关注各州泄露通知法与HIPAA的叠加适用，以及商业伙伴合同中的通报时限约定。

paragraph (b)

314.4 Elements.
In order to develop, implement, and maintain your information security program, you shall:
(a)
Designate a qualified individual responsible for overseeing and implementing your information security program and enforcing your information security program (for purposes of this part, “Qualified Individual”). The Qualified Individual may be employed by you, an affiliate, or a service provider. To the extent the requirement in this
paragraph (a)
is met using a service provider or an affiliate, you shall:
(1)
Retain responsibility for compliance with this part;
(2)
Designate a senior member of your personnel responsible for direction and oversight of the Qualified Individual; and


(3)
Require the service provider or affiliate to maintain an information security program that protects you in accordance with the requirements of this part.
(b)
Base your information security program on a risk assessment that identifies reasonably foreseeable internal and external risks to the security, confidentiality, and integrity of customer information that could result in the unauthorized disclosure, misuse, alteration, destruction, or other compromise of such information, and assesses the sufficiency of any safeguards in place to control these risks.
(1)
The risk assessment shall be written and shall include:


(i)
Criteria for the evaluation and categorization of identified security risks or threats you face;
(
ii
)
Criteria for the assessment of the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of your information systems and customer information, including the adequacy of the existing controls in the context of the identified risks or threats you face; and
(
iii
)
Requirements describing how identified risks will be mitigated or accepted based on the risk assessment and how the information security program will address the risks.


(2)
You shall periodically perform additional risk assessments that reexamine the reasonably foreseeable internal and external risks to the security, confidentiality, and integrity of customer information that could result in the unauthorized disclosure, misuse, alteration, destruction, or other compromise of such information, and reassess the sufficiency of any safeguards in place to control these risks.
(c)
Design and implement safeguards to control the risks you identify through risk assessment, including by:
(1)
Implementing and periodically reviewing access controls, including technical and, as appropriate, physical controls to:


(i)
Authenticate and permit access only to authorized users to protect against the unauthorized acquisition of customer information; and
(
ii
)
Limit authorized users' access only to customer information that they need to perform their duties and functions, or, in the case of customers, to access their own information;
(2)
Identify and manage the data, personnel, devices, systems, and facilities that enable you to achieve business purposes in accordance with their relative importance to business objectives and your risk strategy;


(3)
Protect by encryption all customer information held or transmitted by you both in transit over external networks and at rest. To the extent you determine that encryption of customer information, either in transit over external networks or at rest, is infeasible, you may instead secure such customer information using effective alternative compensating controls reviewed and approved by your Qualified Individual;


(4)
Adopt secure development practices for in-house developed applications utilized by you for transmitting, accessing, or storing customer information and procedures for evaluating, assessing, or testing the security of externally developed applications you utilize to transmit, access, or store customer information;
(5)
Implement multi-factor authentication for any individual accessing any information system, unless your Qualified Individual has approved in writing the use of reasonably equivalent or more secure access controls;

(6)(i)
Develop, implement, and maintain procedures for the secure disposal of customer information in any format no later than two years after the last date the information is used in connection with the provision of a product or service to the customer to which it relates, unless such information is necessary for business operations or for other legitimate business purposes, is otherwise required to be retained by law or regulation, or where targeted disposal is not reasonably feasible due to the manner in which the information is maintained; and
(
ii
)
Periodically review your data retention policy to minimize the unnecessary retention of data;
(7)
Adopt procedures for change management; and


(8)
Implement policies, procedures, and controls designed to monitor and log the activity of authorized users and detect unauthorized access or use of, or tampering with, customer information by such users.
(d)(1)
Regularly test or otherwise monitor the effectiveness of the safeguards' key controls, systems, and procedures, including those to detect actual and attempted attacks on, or intrusions into, information systems.


(2)
For information systems, the monitoring and testing shall include continuous monitoring or periodic penetration testing and vulnerability assessments. Absent effective continuous monitoring or other systems to detect, on an ongoing basis, changes in information systems that may create vulnerabilities, you shall conduct:


(i)
Annual penetration testing of your information systems determined each given year based on relevant identified risks in accordance with the risk assessment; and
(
ii
)
Vulnerability assessments, including any systemic scans or reviews of information systems reasonably designed to identify publicly known security vulnerabilities in your information systems based on the risk assessment, at least every six months; and whenever there are material changes to your operations or business arrangements; and whenever there are circumstances you know or have reason to know may have a material impact on your information security program.


(e)
Implement policies and procedures to ensure that personnel are able to enact your information security program by:
(1)
Providing your personnel with security awareness training that is updated as necessary to reflect risks identified by the risk assessment;
(2)
Utilizing qualified information security personnel employed by you or an affiliate or service provider sufficient to manage your information security risks and to perform or oversee the information security program;
(3)
Providing information security personnel with security updates and training sufficient to address relevant security risks; and


(4)
Verifying that key information security personnel take steps to maintain current knowledge of changing information security threats and countermeasures.
(f)
Oversee service providers, by:
(1)
Taking reasonable steps to select and retain service providers that are capable of maintaining appropriate safeguards for the customer information at issue;
(2)
Requiring your service providers by contract to implement and maintain such safeguards; and
(3)
Periodically assessing your service providers based on the risk they present and the continued adequacy of their safeguards.


(g)
Evaluate and adjust your information security program in light of the results of the testing and monitoring required by
paragraph (d)
of this section; any material changes to your operations or business arrangements; the results of risk assessments performed under
paragraph (b)(2)
of this section; or any other circumstances that you know or have reason to know may have a material impact on your information security program.


(h)
Establish a written incident response plan designed to promptly respond to, and recover from, any security event materially affecting the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of customer information in your control. Such incident response plan shall address the following areas:
(1)
The goals of the incident response plan;
(2)
The internal processes for responding to a security event;
(3)
The definition of clear roles, responsibilities, and levels of decision-making authority;
(4)
External and internal communications and information sharing;


(5)
Identification of requirements for the remediation of any identified weaknesses in information systems and associated controls;
(6)
Documentation and reporting regarding security events and related incident response activities; and
(7)
The evaluation and revision as necessary of the incident response plan following a security event.


(i)
Require your Qualified Individual to report in writing, regularly and at least annually, to your board of directors or equivalent governing body. If no such board of directors or equivalent governing body exists, such report shall be timely presented to a senior officer responsible for your information security program. The report shall include the following information:
(1)
The overall status of the information security program and your compliance with this part; and


(2)
Material matters related to the information security program, addressing issues such as risk assessment, risk management and control decisions, service provider arrangements, results of testing, security events or violations and management's responses thereto, and recommendations for changes in the information security program.
(j)
Notify the Federal Trade Commission about notification events in accordance with
paragraphs (j)(1)
and
(2)
of this section.


(1)
Notification requirement.
Upon discovery of a notification event as described in
paragraph (j)(2)
of this section, if the notification event involves the information of at least 500 consumers, you must notify the Federal Trade Commission as soon as possible, and no later than 30 days after discovery of the event. The notice shall be made electronically on a form to be located on the FTC's website,
https://www.ftc.gov
.
The notice shall include the following:


(i)
The name and contact information of the reporting financial institution;
(
ii
)
A description of the types of information that were involved in the notification event;
(
iii
)
If the information is possible to determine, the date or date range of the notification event;
(
iv
)
The number of consumers affected or potentially affected by the notification event;

(v)
A general description of the notification event; and
(
vi
)
Whether any law enforcement official has provided you with a written determination that notifying the public of the breach would impede a criminal investigation or cause damage to national security, and a means for the Federal Trade Commission to contact the law enforcement official. A law enforcement official may request an initial delay of up to 30 days following the date when notice was provided to the Federal Trade Commission. The delay may be extended for an additional period of up to 60 days if the law enforcement official seeks such an extension in writing.

 Additional delay may be permitted only if the Commission staff determines that public disclosure of a security event continues to impede a criminal investigation or cause damage to national security.

(2)
Notification event treated as discovered.
A notification event shall be treated as discovered as of the first day on which such event is known to you. You shall be deemed to have knowledge of a notification event if such event is known to any person, other than the person committing the breach, who is your employee, officer, or other agent.
